title: Michelle Obama on Striking a Balance Between Job, Motherhood
main_content:
First lady Michelle Obama focused on women striking the elusive work-life balance in an interview with Oprah Winfrey at the first White House summit on the State of Women.

“I had had Malia, Barack was in the U.S. Senate, so I was basically mothering part-time on my own, having, I had a full-time job,” said Obama, recounting the story of negotiating a job as vice president of community outreach for the University of Chicago Hospital.

Like many women, Mrs. Obama thought that negotiating a part-time position would give her more flexibility at home to be a mother.

Obama told the summit of more than 5,000 people, “The only thing I found out from part-time was that you just get paid part-time.”

“So I had vowed that if I continued to work, that I would never settle for part-time,” she said. “I knew what my time and energy was worth.”

questions.question: What did Michelle Obama talk about with Oprah Winfrey during the interview?
options: Her experiences in child-rearing while pursuing a career
The importance of education for women globally
Her views on political leadership and women
The impact of social media on women's issues
questions.answer: Her experiences in child-rearing while pursuing a career

questions.question: What did Mrs. Obama say she found out about working part-time?
options: It allowed her to take on more responsibilities at home
It did not provide the flexibility she anticipated
It was financially equivalent to full-time work
It increased her anxiety about work-life balance
questions.answer: It did not provide the flexibility she anticipated

questions.question: What did Mrs. Obama say she would never settle for if she continued to work?
options: A job at the White House
